newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-Deutsche takes control of MGAM business.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Deutsche takes control of MGAM business.

text.p: Deutsche Bank AG, in a further reaction to recent problems at London fund unit Morgan Grenfell Asset Management, said on Thursday it would seize managerial responsibility for MGAM's unit trust business.

Deutsche management board member, Tessen von Heydebreck, said Deutsche's German asset management arm DWS would take ultimate control of MGAM's fund business for retail clients, but not of its institutional funds business.

The decision follows the discovery of misvaluations at three MGAM European funds in September which prompted Deutsche to consider afresh plans to put its British unit trust business under closer supervision from Frankfurt.

"Ultimate responsibility for MGAM unit trusts will lie with DWS," Heydebreck, who shares responsibility for Deutsche's private customers business, told a news conference. "We at DWS will have risk control."
He did not say when the move would be implemented or what concrete management changes were planned.

Meanwhile, Udo Behrenwaldt, a managing director of DWS Deutsche Gesellschaft fuer Wertpapiersparen mbH, was continuing to travel between London and Frankfurt in his capacity as an adviser to MGAM, DWS said.
Deutsche appointed Behrenwaldt as an adviser in September.

Deutsche's investment banking arm, Morgan Grenfell, last month announced the departure of four key managers after an investigation into misvaluations of speculative unlisted stocks led to the temporary suspension of three funds.
The affair caused worried investors to sell units in the funds back to MGAM, sparking fears that MGAM would run out of cash despite getting a 180 million pounds cash injection from Deutsche.

Heydebreck also said Deutsche expected Britain's investments watchdog IMRO, which is conducting its own investigation into the affair, to reach a decision by year-end on whether investors are due compensation for the loss of value of the three funds.
"We are in the most intensive discussions with IMRO and we both have the firm intention to see this resolved by the end of the year," Heydebreck said.
If IMRO, the Investment Management Regulatory Organisation, finds that MGAM breached rules, it could lead to hefty fines and possible action against individuals.
